text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Kamel Ganzouri says the development process under President Mubarak's leadership achieved at the end of 1996 all that it set out to do, overcoming the challenges it faced.

In the new year, the population will reap the fruits of development and investment in Egypt worth more than 78 billion pounds. The number of private sector projects rose to more than 4,600 in one year.

- Egypt's Capital Markets Authority plans to develop the bourse in the new year. Brokers will be allowed to register their transactions after closing through to 10:00 (0800 GMT) the next morning. There will also be an increase in the number of brokers' screens tied to the bourse.
- President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat spoke by telephone to wish each other happy new year, discuss the peace process and the shooting in Hebron.
- Ganzouri says that Egypt has faced its challenges and succeeded in full development. In the industrial complex in Al-Fayoum there are 600 new projects worth 2.2 billion pounds.

- Sadeq al-Mahdi, former prime minister of Sudan, says that his talks in Egypt with opposition counterparts and Egyptian officials are aimed at understanding the current state of conditions in Sudan and working to achieve the demands of the people.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa will receive former United Nations Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali at the airport on Friday on his return to Egypt from New York at the end of his service.
- Russian submarine passes through the Suez Canal on its way to Iran.
